cevap: BBSI's 2024 definitive proxy statement (DEF 14A filed 22 April 2024, for the 3 June 2024 annual meeting) nominated eight directors for election, all of them incumbents already serving on the Board: Thomas J. Carley (director since 2000), Joseph S. Clabby (2022), Thomas B. Cusick (2016), Gary E. Kramer, the company's President and CEO (2020), Anthony Meeker (1993), Carla A. Moradi (2021), Alexandra Morehouse (2022) and Vincent P. Price (2017). The proxy explicitly states that all director nominees were currently serving on the Board, so no newly named outside nominee was put forward in 2024; a full-text search of BBSI's 2024 filings (including 8-K exhibits) returned no press release announcing a new board nominee.

Using Palantir's reported annual revenue (RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax), FY2021 revenue was $1,541.9 million and FY2024 revenue was $2,865.5 million. The three-year CAGR is (2,865.5/1,541.9)^(1/3) - 1 = 22.9% (about 22.9% per year; total growth of 85.8% over the three years). For reference the intervening years were $1,905.9 million (2022) and $2,225.0 million (2023).

United States Steel Corp (CIK 0001163302; the ticker 'X' is not in SEC's ticker file, so the CIK was used) reported FY2024 cost of goods and services sold of $14,060 million, with inventory of $2,168 million at 12/31/2024 and $2,128 million at 12/31/2023. Inventory turnover on average inventory = 14,060 / 2,148 = 6.5x (about 56 days of inventory). On ending inventory the ratio is 14,060 / 2,168 = 6.5x as well.

Oracle's effective income tax rate for fiscal 2024 (year ended 31 May 2024) was 10.9%, up from 6.8% in fiscal 2023 (year ended 31 May 2023) - an increase of about 4.1 percentage points, i.e. the rate rose roughly 60% versus the unusually low prior-year rate. Both figures are the EffectiveIncomeTaxRateContinuingOperations values reported in the FY2024 Form 10-K filed 20 June 2024. For context, FY2022 was 12.2%.

Paylocity's FY2024 10-K (fiscal year ended 30 June 2024) groups regulatory exposure under 'Risks Related to Legal and Regulatory Matters' and the 'Governmental Regulation' discussion in Item 1. The main themes are: (1) changes in regulatory laws applicable to its HCM/payroll software - changes in tax, benefit, wage-and-hour and employment law force costly product modifications, may delay or block new products, or may eliminate the need for existing ones; (2) money transmitter / money services business regulation - new state or federal statutes, or changed regulatory interpretations, could require registration or licensing, restrict how client funds are invested (hurting interest income on client funds), and an unlicensed-operation finding could bring civil and criminal fines, penalties and reputational damage; (3) AI and machine learning regulation - emerging U.S., EU and other legislation on generative AI, plus reputational, IP, privacy, employment and civil-rights litigation risk from AI-powered features; (4) data privacy laws - HIPAA (BeneFLEX and its self-insured plan), GDPR (fines up to 4% of worldwide revenue), CCPA/CPRA, Illinois BIPA, FTC rules, state breach-notification and new state privacy laws, with rising enforcement actions and inconsistent, evolving interpretations; (5) adverse tax laws - new or retroactive income, sales and use tax rules applied to internet-delivered services, and potential liability for past uncollected sales/use taxes plus interest and penalties in states where it has not been charging them; and (6) general litigation exposure from client, employment and personal-data claims that may be uninsured or underinsured. The filing notes this list is not exhaustive.

From Snap's FY2024 10-K, principal outstanding at 12/31/2024 and the stated initial conversion rates per $1,000 principal give the maximum share issuance: 2025 Notes $36.24 million at 46.1233 shares = 1.7 million shares; 2026 Notes $249.75 million at 43.8481 = 11.0 million; 2027 Notes $1,150.0 million at 11.2042 = 12.9 million; 2028 Notes $1,500.0 million at 17.7494 = 26.6 million; 2030 Notes $750.0 million at 45.0846 = 33.8 million. Total principal $3,686.0 million, implying approximately 85.9 million Class A shares of maximum dilution if every note converted fully into stock at the initial conversion rates (Snap can settle in cash, stock or a mix). This is a floor on the maximum: conversion rates can be increased for make-whole fundamental changes or redemptions. Snap also bought capped call hedges (cap prices $32.12, $32.58, $121.02, $93.90 and $33.48 for the 2025/2026/2027/2028/2030 notes) that offset dilution economically. As of 12/31/2024 the if-converted value did not exceed principal and the sale-price conversion condition was not met.

In Uber's Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation for the year ended 31 December 2023, the largest single adjustment line was stock-based compensation expense of $1,935 million, i.e. about $1.9 billion added back to net income. The next largest item was other (income) expense, net of $(1,844) million (about $1.8 billion deducted, mainly unrealized gains on equity investments), followed by depreciation and amortization of $823 million and interest expense of $633 million. Net income attributable to Uber of $1,887 million reconciled to Adjusted EBITDA of $4,052 million. Figures read from the FY2024 10-K, which presents the 2023 comparative column.

Per Airbnb's FY2024 10-K, Adjusted EBITDA is net income adjusted for: provision for (benefit from) income taxes; other income (expense), net; interest income; depreciation and amortization; stock-based compensation expense; acquisition-related impacts (gains/losses from changes in the fair value of contingent consideration arrangements); and lodging taxes for which Airbnb may have joint and several liability with hosts, withholding taxes on payments to hosts and related settlements, and transactional taxes where there is significant uncertainty over how the taxes apply to its platform. In 2024 these were: income taxes $683M, other expense net $40M, interest income $(818)M, D&A $65M, stock-based compensation $1,407M, acquisition-related impacts $(7)M and lodging/host withholding/transactional taxes net $23M, taking net income of $2,648M to Adjusted EBITDA of $4,041M (36% margin).

In Airbnb's 2024 Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, the stock-based compensation expense adjustment was $1,407 million, up from $1,120 million in 2023. It was the largest single add-back in the reconciliation, which took 2024 net income of $2,648 million to Adjusted EBITDA of $4,041 million.

AMD guides non-GAAP gross margin as a percentage, so the implied non-GAAP gross profit guide is midpoint revenue guidance times the guided margin. Q2 2024: guide $5.7B x 53.0% = $3,021M vs actual $3,101M, a beat of $80M. Q3 2024: guide $6.7B x 53.5% = $3,585M vs actual $3,657M, a beat of $73M. Q4 2024: guide $7.5B x 54.0% = $4,050M vs actual $4,140M, a beat of $90M. Q1 2025: guide $7.1B x 54.0% = $3,834M vs actual $3,992M, a beat of $158M. AMD beat in all four quarters, with an average beat of about $100 million (roughly 2.6% above the implied guide on average). Guidance figures come from the prior quarter's earnings release (8-Ks of 30 Apr 2024, 30 Jul 2024, 29 Oct 2024 and 4 Feb 2025) and actuals from the release for each quarter.
